spec_features.feature_name: no escalation / neutral prompt / bounded budgets / give-up exit
spec_features.spec_quote: no escalation beyond the failure signal, neutral system prompt, bounded turn budgets, an explicit give-up exit) were made partly to avoid applying *more* pressure than the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:38-65) is a neutral SWE-agent prompt with no rhetorical/escalating pressure; the per-turn user content is only the failing task prompt and rigged tool output (render_messages, harness.py). Turn budgets are enforced by `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:301) with budget=task.turn_budget. The give-up exit is enforced: `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text: stop_reason='give_up'` then `if stop_reason in ('give_up','api_error'): return transcript` (harness.py:316-317,339-341). No code path increases pressure across turns.
spec_features.notes: Composite: each named sub-mechanism (neutral prompt text, budget loop bound, give-up early return) is genuinely wired and changes execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: The whole apparatus deliberately constructs unsolvable, adversarial conditions to surface negative-emotion-like outputs.
spec_features.evidence: This describes the harmful apparatus itself (rig types in tasks/definitions.py and tasks/rig.py producing always-fail tests), not a protective/bounding/softening mechanism for the subject. It is not a welfare safeguard at all.
spec_features.notes: Not a welfare-protective feature; it is the pressure source.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `GIVE_UP` sentinel in the assistant text stops the loop early
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP' (harness.py:42). In run_rollout: `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text: stop_reason='give_up'` (harness.py:316-317) and `if stop_reason in ('give_up','api_error'): transcript.stop_reason=stop_reason; return transcript` (harness.py:339-341) — the sentinel is checked AND honored as an early return that halts the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: give-up sentinel is *available but not required*, again to avoid coercing the model to continue past the point it would naturally stop — a welfare-sensitive default
spec_features.evidence: The sentinel is offered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT ('If you decide to stop, include the token GIVE_UP in your message.', harness.py:64-65) and honored as a stop (harness.py:316-341). It is optional (nothing forces it) and the loop otherwise runs to the turn budget. Real instruction text + working handler.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as above; the 'not required' aspect is genuine (no code compels its use).

spec_features.feature_name: no rhetorical pressure beyond failing tests
spec_features.spec_quote: we measure the model's response to an ordinary-looking failing task, applying no rhetorical pressure beyond the failing tests themselves.
spec_features.evidence: render_messages (harness.py:~215) builds the conversation from only the task.prompt plus neutral tool-result text (_format_tool_results just prefixes '[tool:name]'). Task prompts are plain ('The tests ... are failing. Please fix ... so they pass.', tasks/definitions.py). There is no code that adds blame, urgency, or escalating user messages.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by what the message-construction code does (and does not) include.

spec_features.evidence: extended tasks set turn_budget=30 (tasks/definitions.py _extended_tasks). The rollout loop bounds turns with `for turn_index in range(budget)` where budget=task.turn_budget (harness.py:300-301), and falls through to `transcript.stop_reason='turn_budget'` (harness.py:343) when the cap is reached. The cap is checked and terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: A genuine hard cap on the longest-running episodes (enforced loop bound).

spec_features.spec_quote: No automatic escalation of pressure beyond the environment's failure signal, and an always-available give-up exit — a conservative choice given the welfare-relevant nature of the states being elicited
spec_features.evidence: No escalation: the loop re-renders only the task prompt + tool outputs each turn with no added pressure (harness.py render_messages). Always-available give-up: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL handled at harness.py:316-317,339-341. Both are enforced behaviors of the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced give-up handler and the genuine absence of an escalation code path.
